articles.headline: More than 100 companies back major AI cyber-defense push
articles.summary: OpenAI, Anthropic, Microsoft, AMD and more than 100 other companies signed a letter urging businesses and policymakers to prioritize cybersecurity in the age of AI. The business relevance is direct: firms adopting AI tools are being pushed to strengthen defensive controls, and the signal may accelerate enterprise spending on security and governance.

articles.headline: EU AI Act transparency rules now apply to businesses using AI in the EU
articles.summary: The EU AI Act’s transparency obligations began applying on 2 August 2026 to businesses that develop or deploy AI systems whose outputs are intended for use in the EU. Companies operating in Europe now need to review disclosure, labeling, and governance processes, or face compliance and operational risk.

articles.headline: China’s CXMT posts sharp turnaround as memory demand surges
articles.summary: CXMT’s swing to profit highlights how AI-driven demand is lifting memory prices and reshaping chip supply dynamics. That matters for companies that rely on servers, cloud infrastructure and device supply chains because memory costs can affect capital spending and deployment timelines.
